items.title: Author's own checklist states a real CMake/CPack build has not been performed

findings.title: Author's own checklist states a real CMake/CPack build has not been performed
findings.evidence: 1. Perform a **real** CMake extension configuration, build and CPack packaging using an installed matching Slicer SDK/build tree or the Slicer extension build infrastructure. The mock configuration does **not** prove that Slicer can build and package this extension.
findings.explanation: The committed CMake files look conventional (slicerMacroBuildScriptedModule with the .py and .ui listed), but the author documents that only a mock configuration was run, so it is unverified that the package builds and that the module loads from the installed package.
findings.suggestion: Confirm a successful extension build/package (or CI build) before merge and update the checklist accordingly.

findings.title: Real CMake/CPack build not verified by the author
findings.evidence: 1. Perform a **real** CMake extension configuration, build and CPack packaging using an installed matching Slicer SDK/build tree or the Slicer extension build infrastructure. The mock configuration does **not** prove that Slicer can build and package this extension.
findings.explanation: The submission checklist states that only a mock CMake configuration was run, and that a real Slicer-SDK build and package are still required. The entry may therefore fail to build in the index infrastructure.
findings.suggestion: Rely on the index's CI build results for the PR; confirm the build passes before merge.

items.title: Catalog entry tracks a moving branch instead of a pinned revision

findings.title: Catalog entry tracks a moving branch instead of a pinned revision
findings.explanation: scm_revision is 'main', so the built extension can change without a catalog update. The reviewed source is therefore not fixed. The policy allows branch references, but a tagged release revision would make the reviewed build reproducible.
findings.suggestion: Pin scm_revision to a tagged release or commit hash for the reviewed baseline (v0.6.84).

items.title: HD-BET and vesselness run synchronously on the GUI thread with processEvents

findings.title: HD-BET and vesselness run synchronously on the GUI thread with processEvents
findings.explanation: run_hd_bet(...) is called directly from the button handler (line 13439) and can take minutes on CPU. Because processEvents() is pumped before the call, the UI stays interactive and the user can trigger other module actions (segmentation edits, scene changes) while the input volume is being written and read back, which can produce inconsistent results or re-entrant state. The same pattern applies to the vesselness and Wrap Solidify paths.
findings.suggestion: Move HD-BET and full-volume vesselness into a slicer.util.ProgressDialog / CLI-style worker or a background thread, disable the relevant controls while running, and report progress instead of pumping the event loop.

items.title: No automated tests in the extension

findings.title: No automated tests in the extension
findings.explanation: A search for 'ScriptedLoadableModuleTest' and 'def runTest' over the repository returned no matches, so none of the registration, segmentation or 3D-view logic is covered by Slicer's extension test harness. Regressions in a 24k-line single file will only be caught manually.
findings.suggestion: Add a minimal ScriptedLoadableModuleTest that loads the module, creates a synthetic volume and exercises at least one non-optional workflow.

items.title: README asserts the extension is already accepted into the Extensions Index

findings.title: README asserts the extension is already accepted into the Extensions Index
findings.evidence: The extension was accepted into the official [3D Slicer Extensions Index](https://github.com/Slicer/ExtensionsIndex/blob/main/NeurosurgicalPlanning.json) when [PR #2413](https://github.com/Slicer/ExtensionsIndex/pull/2413) was merged on **October 16, 2026**.
findings.explanation: The README tells users the extension is already published and installable from the Extension Manager, which pre-empts the outcome of this review and cannot be verified from the repository. If the entry is not merged, users following the installation instructions will not find the package.
findings.suggestion: Reword to describe the submission as pending until the catalog entry is actually merged, or state the claim only after merge.

items.title: Silent exception swallowing during temp-file cleanup

findings.title: Silent exception swallowing during temp-file cleanup
findings.explanation: In the HD-BET finally block, errors from os.remove are caught and discarded, so a failed cleanup of patient-derived temporary NIfTI files in the temp directory goes unreported. This is low-impact, but it hides cleanup failures.
findings.suggestion: Log the exception with logging.warning, or narrow it to OSError.

items.title: HD-BET dependency setup is delegated to the HDBrainExtraction extension on user action

findings.title: HD-BET dependency setup is delegated to the HDBrainExtraction extension on user action
findings.evidence:
from HDBrainExtractionTool import HDBrainExtractionToolLogic
                dependencyLogic = HDBrainExtractionToolLogic()
                dependencyLogic.setupPythonRequirements()
findings.explanation: This call can install Python packages (including PyTorch via that extension's PyTorchUtils path) into Slicer's environment. It is only reached when the user presses the HD-BET button and the installation logic belongs to the HDBrainExtraction extension, so it is not a violation of the PyTorch policy, but users should be told that pressing the button may install packages.
findings.suggestion: Mention in the UI/README that the first HD-BET run may install Python packages through the HDBrainExtraction extension.

items.title: Large binary screenshots committed to the repository

findings.title: Large binary screenshots committed to the repository
findings.explanation: Three PNGs of roughly 0.45-1.6 MB each (~3.5 MB total) are committed. This is acceptable for documentation but inflates every clone of the extension source.
findings.suggestion: Optionally downscale the screenshots or host them outside the source tree.

items.title: Large single-file module and long GUI-thread operations

findings.title: Large single-file module and long GUI-thread operations
findings.explanation: SurgicalPlanning.py is about 24,000 lines in one file. HD-BET and Wrap Solidify run synchronously on the GUI thread, with only processEvents calls for progress. This affects maintainability and responsiveness, not safety.
findings.suggestion: Consider splitting the module and running heavy inference off the GUI thread with progress reporting.

findings.title: Single 1 MB / 24k-line module file
findings.explanation: All logic, UI wiring and algorithms live in one file of 24357 lines, which makes review, testing and maintenance difficult and increases the chance that unrelated workflows break together.
findings.suggestion: Consider splitting logic into separate modules (registration, segmentation, vesselness, 3D view) in a future release.
